challenge: OpenCode Go Open Research Challenge (prediction + biomarkers, 412 cohort)

screening_protocol.description: Every candidate predictor was blended with R0 under an honest nested protocol: the blend weight (and any candidate hyperparameters) were selected only on a 3-fold inner OOF within the outer-training scope; the outer-test fold remained untouched.

decisive_falsification.screen: screen #8: fixed-representation subject-relative ridge blend vs architecture-matched global-standardization control, fresh seeds 16-20
decisive_falsification.conclusion: FI fails P1 (-0.0012 < +0.005); the small WM gain is matched by its architecture-matched control (+0.0062), so the novel subject-relative representation adds no information beyond a heavy-ridge blend (a rejected 'different lambda' variant).

screen7_joint_selection.conclusion: Joint selection of representation, alpha, and weight on noisy inner OOF destroys the apparent gains.

bank_screen_examples.conclusion: WM-side families exist but do not transfer to FI; FI-side families are seed-unstable.

reason_for_rejection: Across 9 screens and ~60 genuinely distinct candidate predictors evaluated with honest nested blending on 10 fresh screening seeds, no method improved BOTH WM and FI by the predeclared +0.005 margin with the required seed stability. WM-side improvements (up to +0.05) never transferred to FI, and the one apparent FI-side signal (subject-relative normalization) failed to replicate on fresh seeds and was matched by its architecture-matched control. Running a locked evaluation of any candidate would be a cosmetic variant prohibited by the challenge rules.
